_comment: Per-fixture worst-page tolerances for the generated IDML/PDF corpus.
Each fixture's renderer-vs-pdftoppm output is gated on these numbers in
CI (.github/workflows/fidelity.yml -> corpus/generated/diff.sh).
Semantics: a fixture passes iff *every* page that has a matching
reference PDF page (cand-NNN.png + ref-NNN.png) satisfies
mean_de <= max_mean_de AND p99_de <= max_p99_de AND ssim >= min_ssim.
Pages without a matching reference are skipped (max_pages_with_pdf bounds
this — IDMLs that grew past their last InDesign-export are still allowed
to run; only the first N pages are gated).
Calibration: thresholds were originally sized to the worst observed page
+ ~15-25% headroom so noise does not flap. They are periodically
*tightened* (never loosened to mask a regression) so a fixture running
well below its budget actually catches future regressions.
Tightening rule of thumb:
worst_current / threshold ratio  →  action
> 75%                          →  leave alone (close to the edge)
50–75%                         →  drop to worst * 1.15 (15% headroom)
≤ 50%                          →  drop to worst * 1.20 (20% headroom)
SSIM is raised toward (worst_min - ~0.005) once there is ≥0.010 headroom.
Long-term goal stays the idea.md §13.2 budget:
mean ΔE <= 1.0, p99 ΔE <= 2.5, SSIM >= 0.99 (every page).
Tightening below those targets needs a (now generously achieved) measurement
to justify it; loosening any threshold needs a written rationale in the
commit message.

fixtures.name: layout
fixtures.rationale: Re-gated 2026-09-10 for the column wave. Two changes pull in opposite directions and both are recorded here. TIGHTER: p99 59.11 -> 54.38, because layout.fonts.sh now registers Inter — the fixture sets its body copy in Inter (samples/layout.rs BODY_FONT) and the harness default registered only Open Sans + Minion Pro, so every body run fell back to SourceSerif4 while InDesign exported it in Inter. Pages 1-4 improved on that alone (0.417/0.524/0.457/0.902 -> 0.154/0.218/0.251/0.582). LOOSER: mean 1.083 -> 1.302 and ssim 0.9502 -> 0.939, NOT to mask a regression but because the fixture gained four pages (7-10, the column cases) carrying 44 lines of body copy each — denser than anything it held before, so the worst page moved from page 4 (0.902) to page 10 (1.132). Worst across all 10 pages: mean 1.132 / p99 47.289 / ssim 0.944; sized at worst * 1.15 and worst_ssim - 0.005. Page 11 (2col-autosize-height) joined the gate 2026-09-11 and moved NO threshold: it measures mean 0.363 / p99 15.627 / ssim 0.987, well inside the values above, so only max_pages_with_pdf changed. It is gated because the rule it pins is a MEASURED one — InDesign grows a two-column auto-height frame to ten lines and splits 10/10, where we grew it to twenty in one full-width column. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.636 / p99 47.289 / ssim 0.9605 (was 1.132 / 47.289 / 0.9441); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: swatches
fixtures.rationale: New 2026-09-08. Spot ink at full strength, the same ink at 50% through the object's FillTint, and a frame whose paint comes from its applied ObjectStyle with no inline FillColor. Was measuring worst mean 31.8 / SSIM 0.70 because the generator wrote four things InDesign does not: a spot whose CMYK alternate differs from its Lab primary (all 15 corpus spots are LAB/LAB and identical), TintValue on a <Color> (0 of 7,545), a <Swatch Color=...> alias (<Swatch> is Swatch/None 271 of 271 times), and BasedOn on an ObjectStyle (0 of 1,101 — InDesign flattens the inheritance at export). Now worst page mean 0.142 / p99 0.212 / SSIM 0.9997.

Reference re-exported from the changed IDML; all 13 pages gated (was 7). Worst page mean 0.219 / p99 2.457 / SSIM 0.9878 - tightened from 1.1/13.0/0.96, which had made this the loosest fixture in the corpus. Against the honest reference the worst page measures mean 0.390 / p99 0.198 / SSIM 0.982 (p6, the densest text page); the PDF also grew 13→19 pages, so every page is gated now. Budget = measured × ~1.25 with p99 left a 1.0 noise floor. The DROP CAP that dominated p1 is measured and fixed — size, ink flush and body indent all match InDesign to under a point. Worst page is still p1 at mean 0.634 / p99 21.5 / SSIM 0.970, and what remains there is a LINE BREAK: the third line keeps a word InDesign moves on. Our advances are right (the same text sets within 0.8 pt over a 414 pt line, measured against InDesign's own `story.lines`), so the difference is the composer's objective, not its measure. Budget = measured x ~1.2. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.587 / p99 16.554 / ssim 0.9730 (was 0.634 / 21.479 / 0.9700); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: start-paragraph
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with ADR 028 (the break-before rule, StartParagraph). Ten cases, each one story threaded through a four-page chain (a two-column frame and a one-column frame on page 1, one frame on each of pages 2-4), every case starting on an odd page; the reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and where each case's rule paragraph lands matches it (also pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/start_paragraph_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.130 / p99 0.0 / ssim 0.9884; sized at worst * 1.20, the p99 at the 0.3 floor other fixtures use, ssim worst - 0.005. Body copy is Inter, registered by start-paragraph.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.103 / p99 0.000 / ssim 0.9893 (was 0.130 / 0.000 / 0.9882); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: forced-line-break
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with the forced line break (U+2028, core ab383b1). Seven cases on one page (indent + spacing, bullets, numbers, two breaks in a row, a break that ends the paragraph, justified, a break that starts it); the reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and every line of every case lands where InDesign put it (also pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/forced_line_break_pipeline.rs). It could join only once the importer kept U+2028 in the run (plugin-publish 18d0622): while it folded the break into \n the gate rendered every break as a paragraph mark and measured mean 0.757 / p99 26.6. Worst page measured: mean 0.591 / p99 12.611 / ssim 0.9470; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE at the time, not the forced break: in the bullets and numbers cases the text after the list marker started at the wrong x (the engine puts a space after an undeclared BulletsTextAfter where InDesign's default is a tab, and the number's tab lands at 108 pt, the next 36 pt default stop, instead of the hanging indent's left indent at 90 pt); with those two frames masked the page measures mean 0.387. Body copy is Inter, registered by forced-line-break.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 once that residue was fixed (core: an undeclared BulletsTextAfter is a tab, and a hanging first line's left indent is a tab stop; measured by the list-markers fixture): the page now measures mean 0.506 / p99 12.611 / ssim 0.9519, re-sized at worst * 1.20 (p99 unchanged at 15.13) and worst_ssim - 0.005. What remains is not the list markers: the 0.25 pt frame strokes and glyph-edge antialiasing (the 0.387 above was with whole frames masked, strokes included). TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.421 / p99 12.611 / ssim 0.9546 (was 0.506 / 12.611 / 0.9519); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: list-markers
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign where the text after a list marker starts. Fourteen cases on one page, two paragraphs each: BulletsTextAfter undeclared / ^t / a space; NumberingExpression ^#.^t / ^#.; no indent, left indent only, hanging indents (one narrower than the number), explicit tab stops before, beyond and under the marker, and a plain tab in a hanging paragraph with no list. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export, and the x of the text after every marker matches it within 0.5 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/list_markers_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.873 / p99 33.344 / ssim 0.9096; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. The residue is not the markers: fourteen 0.25 pt frame strokes the CPU rasteriser paints lighter than InDesign, plus glyph-edge antialiasing (before the fix the page measured mean 1.114 / p99 53.7 / ssim 0.8958). Body copy is Inter, registered by list-markers.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.642 / p99 12.611 / ssim 0.9206 (was 0.873 / 33.344 / 0.9096); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: list-overrides
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign how the list attributes behave when set on the paragraph range itself rather than in its style. Twenty-two cases, two paragraphs each: BulletsTextAfter / NumberingExpression as local attributes, as typed <Properties> children, and over a style that says otherwise; NumberingStartAt / NumberingContinue on the first, the second and through a style (including InDesign's own [No paragraph style] pair start 1 + continue true); NumberingFormat as child and as attribute; the marker character styles as children and as attributes. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; the text after every marker and the marker's width (which tells the counter values apart) match it within 0.5 / 0.1 pt in all 22 cases, pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/list_markers_pipeline.rs. Worst page measured: mean 1.132 / p99 51.432 / ssim 0.8958 (tightened 2026-10-01 from 1.218 / 62.710 / 0.8919 when the marker character style's size and face were honoured); sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. Residue: the same 0.25 pt frame strokes and glyph-edge antialiasing as list-markers, over 22 frames instead of 14. Body copy is Inter, registered by list-overrides.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.809 / p99 17.397 / ssim 0.9077 (was 1.132 / 51.432 / 0.8958); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: list-marker-styles
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign what a list marker's character style does to the marker. Twenty-two cases, two paragraphs each: a BulletsCharacterStyle / NumberingCharacterStyle that sets size, family (JetBrains Mono), bold, colour, baseline shift, tracking, or nothing, each for a bullet and a number; a 20 pt marker under auto leading, before a tab, from the paragraph style, and over a run with its own bold / colour. InDesign's rule: the whole marker (number, literal and separator) takes the character style laid over the first character's formatting, the style winning over the run's local values, and the marker never raises the line's auto leading. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; every line's baseline, the text after the marker, and each marker glyph's position, size and colour match it within 0.5 / 0.1 pt, pinned by crates/paged-renderer/tests/list_markers_pipeline.rs. Worst page measured: mean 1.079 / p99 50.589 / ssim 0.8976; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. Residue: the same 0.25 pt frame strokes and glyph-edge antialiasing as list-overrides. Body copy is Inter and one marker style JetBrains Mono, registered by list-marker-styles.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.804 / p99 16.445 / ssim 0.9078 (was 1.079 / 50.589 / 0.8976); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: span-columns
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with span and split columns (SpanColumnType, SpanSplitColumnCount, SpanColumnMinSpaceBefore/After, SplitColumnInsideGutter/OutsideGutter). Seventeen cases, one per page, each one story threaded through two frames (spans in 2- and 3-column frames: at the story's start, mid-story, over 2 of 3 columns with overflow into the third column and frame B, with min space and SpaceBefore/After in both orders, with no room left, centred; splits into 2 and 3 in a 1-column frame and inside one column of a 2-column frame, with default and explicit gutters, min space, a paragraph straddling the split, and a block crossing into frame B). The reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and all 256 lines land where InDesign put them, within 0.13 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/span_columns_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.203 / p99 0.210 / ssim 0.9830; sized at worst * 1.20, the p99 at the 0.3 floor other fixtures use, ssim worst - 0.005. Body copy is Inter, registered by span-columns.fonts.sh. fixtures.name: split-boundaries
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 with split-block boundaries: where one block of SplitColumns paragraphs ends and the next begins. Twenty-four cases in span-columns' page layout (one story through frames A and B, Inter 10/12, numbered one-line paragraphs): consecutive splits with a different count (2 then 3, 3 then 2), inside gutter, outside gutter, min space only, and spelled-out defaults; a split directly before and after a span; block boundaries across a column, across a frame, and at a full frame; and the spacing at a boundary (min space after vs before, SpaceAfter + SpaceBefore, with and without min space, single text either side). The reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and all 306 lines land where InDesign put them, within 0.12 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/span_columns_pipeline.rs). fixtures.name: tab-breaks
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign where a line breaks when a tab decides it (core: the composer measures each tab at the width it takes on its line, paged_text::layout::tab_aware_breaks). Page 1: fourteen cases with a tab near the right edge of a 200 pt frame (a left stop the next word no longer fits after, a stop the word after the tab cannot fit at, default and explicit stops exceeding the measure, right/decimal/center stops near the edge, a tab past the last explicit stop, a stop beyond the frame, justified text with a tab). Page 2: Left/Right/Center/Decimal minimum-width sweeps and edge probes. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; every asserted word sits on InDesign's line within 0.5 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/tab_breaks_pipeline.rs). Before the change the pages measured mean 0.801 / p99 28.53 / ssim 0.9625 (page 1) and 0.476 / 14.53 / 0.9820 (page 2); after, worst page mean 0.403 / p99 13.177 / ssim 0.9842; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE, not the tab rule: c09's tab-free last line (InDesign sets its spaces at 70 %, below the 80 % minimum, to keep one word the engine wraps) and two edge probes InDesign keeps on the line by squeezing a 0.1 pt overflow. Frames carry no stroke: InDesign insets a frame's text by half a centre-aligned stroke. Body copy is Inter, registered by tab-breaks.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.176 / p99 3.202 / ssim 0.9942 (was 0.403 / 13.177 / 0.9842); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: stroke-inset
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign how a text frame's stroke moves its text. Thirty-one one-frame cases on two pages (Inter 10/12, LeadingOffset, hyphenation off; one-line paragraphs alternating left/right): stroke weights 0.25 / 1 / 6 / 12 pt at centre / inside / outside, a stroke with no colour, InsetSpacing plus a stroke, frames whose height lets the stroke decide whether the fifth line fits, two-column frames, rounded corners and a chamfered polygon. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; its rule (a painted stroke insets the text area on all four sides by half its weight centred, all of it inside, none outside, on top of InsetSpacing; the gutter is unchanged) is pinned line by line within 0.05 pt by crates/paged-renderer/tests/stroke_inset_pipeline.rs. Worst page measured: mean 4.025 / p99 84.138 / ssim 0.8960; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (a text frame's StrokeAlignment reaches the model, plugin-publish 2ab572b, and the renderer strokes the outline it names): the twelve inside / outside frames, which were painted and inset as centred, now paint and set where InDesign does (pinned within 0.05 pt); worst page mean 4.025 -> 0.534, p99 84.138 -> 8.891, ssim 0.8960 -> 0.9724 (page 2), all <= 50% of the old budget, so sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE: the rounded-corner frames (the engine does not lay text out around corner effects); and shaped frames, which the engine does not inset by their stroke yet (see text_area_frame). Body copy is Inter, registered by stroke-inset.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (shaped frames are inset by their stroke too, and the chamfered cases 27-30 land on InDesign's lines): worst page now mean 0.228 / p99 4.474 / ssim 0.9872 (was 0.534 / 8.893 / 0.9724); mean and p99 x1.20 (<=50%), ssim worst - 0.005.

fixtures.name: shaped-bands
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign how lines fit SHAPED text frames. Eighteen frames on three pages (Inter 10/12, hyphenation off): a circle, an apex-up triangle, a square donut whose hole splits the middle rows, a chamfered rectangle, a rectangle with a notch (every edge on a whole point) and a narrow ellipse, set left / right / centred / justified, AscentOffset and LeadingOffset, with insets and painted strokes. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; every line (text, ink start / end, baseline) is pinned within 0.05 pt by crates/paged-renderer/tests/shaped_bands_pipeline.rs. Worst page measured: mean 0.455 / p99 12.393 / ssim 0.9911 (the engine before the band rules: 5.848 / 84.138 / 0.7260); sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE: the justified donut (InDesign letterspaces a lone word across its part of a split row) and one line of the stroked circle (1 pt). Body copy is Inter, registered by shaped-bands.fonts.sh.
